label: Item itself (access)
summary: Gives back the infected-province entry itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses the same name on other types (`PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` handed to another function), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Infection progress
summary: The infection progress of one infected province in the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a widget in the epidemics window, so the widget shows the progress data. What exactly the value holds (a number, a bar) is not documented.

label: Province
summary: The province this infected-province entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the epidemics window, so the widget can show that province.

label: Item itself
summary: The infected-province entry itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types (for example `recipient.Self` passed as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Realm entry itself (access)
summary: Gives back the infected-realm entry itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Average infection
summary: The average infection rate for this infected realm, as a number.
details: The epidemics window shows it as a percentage in a tooltip line "Average infection rate in <title name>".

label: Infected provinces
summary: The list of infected provinces (baronies) in this realm.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a window repeats a row for, and counts its entries to show "Infected baronies: N". What kind of item each entry is is not stated by the input.

label: Realm title
summary: The title that this infected-realm entry belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the epidemics window, so the widget can show that title.

label: Widget size
summary: The width and height a widget of the epidemics window should have for this realm entry.
details: Vanilla sets a widget's `size` from it. Why the size differs between entries is not documented.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether this realm's row in the epidemics window is unfolded.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the window, and to pick frame 1 or 2 of a widget. "Unfolded" is read from the name.

label: Realm entry itself
summary: The infected-realm entry itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Toggle expanded
summary: Unfolds the realm's row in the epidemics window, or folds it again.
details: Vanilla runs it when a widget of the epidemics window is clicked. Going by its name it only switches the expanded state of the realm entry.

label: Infection itself (access)
summary: Gives back the infection object itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: End date
summary: The end date of this infection.
details: Going by its name and its return type (a date), and the way vanilla uses `GetEndDate` on other types (for example `GetEndDate.GetStringShort`). Nothing in vanilla uses it with this type.

label: Infection rate
summary: The infection rate of this infection, as a number.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. A map tooltip shows an "Infection Rate" line using a related epidemic function, not this one.

label: Start date
summary: The date this infection began.
details: Going by its name and its return type (a date), and the way vanilla uses `GetStartDate` on other types (for example `GetStartDate.GetYear`). Nothing in vanilla uses it with this type.

label: Infection itself
summary: The infection object itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Infection level itself (access)
summary: Gives back the infection level itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: County modifier text
summary: The text describing the county modifiers that come with this infection level.
details: Vanilla puts it in a localization text of the epidemics window, below a heading made from the county modifiers text.

label: Province modifier text
summary: The text describing the province modifiers that come with this infection level.
details: Vanilla puts it in a localization text of the epidemics window, below a heading made from the province modifiers text.

label: Realm modifier text
summary: The text describing the realm modifiers that come with this infection level.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the epidemics window and in the county view.

label: Threshold
summary: The infection rate threshold of this level, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in the level names: "Under X%" for the first level and "Over X%" for the others.

label: Has county modifier
summary: Whether this infection level brings county modifiers.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether to show the modifier section and the county modifier text.

label: Has province modifier
summary: Whether this infection level brings province modifiers.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether to show the modifier section and the province modifier text.

label: Has realm modifier
summary: Whether this infection level brings realm modifiers.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the realm modifier text in the epidemics window and the county view.

label: Infection level itself
summary: The infection level itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Epidemic type itself (access)
summary: Gives back the epidemic type itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Custom text
summary: Runs a named custom text for the epidemic type and returns the resulting text.
details: It takes one argument, the name of the custom text. Vanilla uses `Custom('...')` this way on characters; no use with this epidemic type exists, so which names work here is not shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text to run.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of this epidemic type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `texture` of a widget in the shared button and icon GUI file, so it gives the picture to draw.

label: Index
summary: The position number of this epidemic type in the game's list of epidemic types.
details: Going by its name and its whole-number return type, and vanilla's use of `GetIndex` on other types. Nothing in vanilla uses it with this type.

label: Infection levels
summary: The list of infection levels this epidemic type has.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the epidemics window repeats a row for. The input does not say what kind of item each entry is; going by the names, an infection level.

label: Key
summary: The key (script name) of this epidemic type, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type, and vanilla's use of `GetKey` on other types (building keys, for example). Nothing in vanilla uses it with this type.

label: Epidemic name
summary: The name of the kind of epidemic, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts about a new outbreak ("... outbreak appears in ..."), after its intensity.

label: Trait
summary: The trait that this epidemic gives to the people it infects.
details: Vanilla chains it with `.GetName( GetPlayer )` in epidemic tooltips: "has infected you with <trait>" and "Chance of contracting <trait>".

label: Has county modifiers
summary: Whether this epidemic type has county modifiers.
details: Vanilla combines it with the province check (either one is enough) to decide whether to show a part of the epidemics window. How the modifiers are tied to the infection levels is not stated here.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether this epidemic type has an icon.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `HasIcon` on other types to show an icon only if one exists; nothing uses it with this type.

label: Has province modifiers
summary: Whether this epidemic type has province modifiers.
details: Vanilla combines it with the county check (either one is enough) to decide whether to show a part of the epidemics window. How the modifiers are tied to the infection levels is not stated here.

label: Has realm modifiers
summary: Whether this epidemic type has realm modifiers.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a realm-modifier part of the epidemics window. How the modifiers are tied to the infection levels is not stated here.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether this epidemic type is valid.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of `IsValid` on other types. Nothing uses it with this type, and the game does not say what makes one valid.

label: Localize
summary: Looks up a localization key and returns its text.
details: It takes one argument, the key of the text. Vanilla's other `Localize( ... )` uses build a key and return its text. No use with this epidemic type exists.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The localization key to look up.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the epidemic type into a script scope, so script values and scripted texts can work with it.
details: It is a promote: it leads from the interface object into script. Vanilla chains `MakeScope.ScriptValue('...')` on the player in building tooltips; no use with this type exists.

label: Epidemic type itself
summary: The epidemic type itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Focused epidemic's realms
summary: The list of infected realms of the focused epidemic of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows, and checks with it whether the list has any items. "Focused" is read from the name; the window also has a "has focused epidemic" check.

label: Focused epidemic's own infections
summary: The list of own-realm infections of the focused epidemic of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows and checks whether it has any items. What "own realm" covers is read from the name only.

label: Window itself (access)
summary: Gives back the epidemics window itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Clear focused epidemic
summary: Clears the focused epidemic of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click in the epidemics window. Going by its name, nothing is focused afterwards.

label: Close
summary: Closes the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the close button is clicked.

label: Focused area heading
summary: A heading text for the focused area of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text widget in the epidemics window. What the area is is not documented.

label: Focused epidemic
summary: The epidemic that is currently selected in the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window, and calls `ZoomCameraTo` on it from a click. Going by that name, this moves the camera to the epidemic.

label: Focused epidemic's domain infections
summary: The list of domain infections of the focused epidemic of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows and checks whether it has any items. What "domain" covers is read from the name only.

label: Nearby epidemics
summary: The list of epidemics shown in the "nearby" section of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows, and tests whether it is empty together with the window variable `expand_epidemics_nearby`, which controls the section.

label: Other epidemics
summary: The list of epidemics shown in the "world" section of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows, and tests whether it is empty together with the window variable `expand_epidemics_world`. Going by the function name these are the "other" epidemics.

label: Own realm epidemics
summary: The list of epidemics shown in the "own realm" section of the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list for rows, and tests whether it is empty together with the window variable `expand_epidemics_realm`, which controls the section.

label: Has focused epidemic
summary: Whether an epidemic is currently selected in the epidemics window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the detail parts of the window only while one is selected.

label: Select epidemic (other)
summary: Selects the epidemic at a given position in the "other epidemics" list as the focused one.
details: Vanilla passes the row's own position, `PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`, when the row is clicked.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of the epidemic in the list.
fields.values: in vanilla the clicked row's position (`PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`)

label: Select epidemic (own realm)
summary: Selects the epidemic at a given position in the "own realm epidemics" list as the focused one.
details: Vanilla passes the row's own position, `PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`, when the row is clicked.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of the epidemic in the list.
fields.values: in vanilla the clicked row's position (`PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`)

label: Select epidemic (nearby)
summary: Selects the epidemic at a given position in the "nearby epidemics" list as the focused one.
details: Vanilla passes the row's own position, `PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`, when the row is clicked.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of the epidemic in the list.
fields.values: in vanilla the clicked row's position (`PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`)

label: Window itself
summary: The epidemics window itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Ethnicity itself (access)
summary: Gives back the ethnicity itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Name
summary: The display name of the ethnicity, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a button in the ruler designer's ethnicity list.

label: Portrait group
summary: The portrait group the ethnicity belongs to.
details: The ruler designer compares it with the portrait group of the ethnicity chosen now, to show only ethnicities of the same group.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the ethnicity may be shown in the ruler designer's list.
details: Vanilla combines it with the portrait group check, so an ethnicity is listed only if it is visible and in the right group.

label: Ethnicity itself
summary: The ethnicity itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to `RulerDesignerWindow.SetEthnicity` to choose that ethnicity, and compares it with the current one to mark the chosen button.

label: Chain entry itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event chain progress entry itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Index
summary: The position number of this step in the event chain progress.
details: Going by its name and its whole-number return type, and vanilla's use of `GetIndex` on other types. Nothing in vanilla uses it with this type.

label: Is current step
summary: Whether this step of the event chain is the one being done right now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of a part of the event chain progress widget, next to the done and not-done checks. "Current step" is read from the name.

label: Is done
summary: Whether this step of the event chain is already finished.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the "done" look of the step in the chain progress widget of the event window.

label: Is not done
summary: Whether this step of the event chain is not finished yet.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the "not done" look of the step in the chain progress widget of the event window.

label: Chain entry itself
summary: The event chain progress entry itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Event info itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event info entry itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: As-who info
summary: A text with the "as who" information of the event.
details: Vanilla shows it as a line in the debug watch window. The exact content is not documented.

label: Date
summary: The date of the event, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a line in the debug watch window.

label: Name
summary: The name of the event, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a line in the debug watch window.

label: Event info itself
summary: The event info entry itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Layer itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event layer itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The type is for the game's entity editor; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has keyframes
summary: Whether this layer has keyframes.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it, and it belongs to the game's entity editor.

label: Is hovered
summary: Whether the mouse is over this layer.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of `IsHovered` on other types (a highlight while hovered). Nothing uses it with this type.

label: Keyframes
summary: The keyframes of this layer.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it, and it belongs to the game's entity editor.

label: Layer itself
summary: The event layer itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Set hovered
summary: Marks this layer as hovered, or not.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it, and it belongs to the game's entity editor.

label: Option itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event option itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Debug open
summary: Opens a debug view of the event option.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs `EventWindowData.DebugOpen` on a right click in the event window, a similar function of another type. Nothing uses this one.

label: Effects
summary: The list of effects shown for this event option.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that the event windows repeat a row for. Going by its name, the entries are the effects of the option.

label: Click sound
summary: The sound played when this event option is clicked.
details: Vanilla sets a button's `clicksound` from it in the event windows.

label: Text
summary: The text of this event option, as shown on its button.
details: Vanilla shows it as the option's button text, and also compares it with a window variable for tooltips.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this event option.
details: Vanilla shows it as the option's tooltip, and only shows a tooltip when this text is not empty.

label: Has flag
summary: Whether the event option carries a given flag.
details: Vanilla checks the flag `'dangerous'`; for options without it, the tooltip adds the "select this option" shortcut hint.

label: Is timeout option
summary: Whether this option is the one chosen automatically when the event times out.
details: Vanilla combines it with a multiplayer check and a days-remaining check (30 or fewer) to show a warning in the event window.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether this event option is valid.
details: Vanilla shows the "select this option" shortcut hint only for valid options that lack the `dangerous` flag. The game does not say what makes an option valid.

label: On mouse enter
summary: Tells the option that the mouse has entered it.
details: Vanilla runs it on `onmousehierarchyenter` in the event windows, together with the matching `OnLeave`.

label: On mouse leave
summary: Tells the option that the mouse has left it.
details: Vanilla runs it on `onmousehierarchyleave` in the event windows, together with the matching `OnEnter`.

label: Reasons
summary: The list of reasons shown for this event option, such as why it cannot be chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the event windows repeat rows over. What the reasons contain is read from the name.

label: Select
summary: Chooses this event option.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of an option in the event windows.

label: Option itself
summary: The event option itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to `EventWindowViewInsert.OnMouseEnterOption` when the mouse enters an option.

label: Context itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event target setup context itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Variable lists
summary: The variable lists of the event targets set up for a script run.
details: Vanilla reaches it only in the engine's script runner inspector, through ScriptRunnerInspector.AccessEventTargets, and shows the lists there.

label: Variables
summary: The variables of the event targets set up for a script run.
details: Vanilla reaches it only in the engine's script runner inspector, through ScriptRunnerInspector.AccessEventTargets, and shows the variables there.

label: Context itself
summary: The event target setup context itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Event window data
summary: The data of the event shown in this event window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the event window's visual effect widgets (double vision, candlelight and others).

label: Window itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event window itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is on top
summary: Whether this event window is the topmost one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `enabled` condition of widgets, so they work only while the window is on top, and its negation in a `trigger_when` condition.

label: Reset contents
summary: Resets the contents of the event window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a button click in the event windows (the duel event and the shared event window file). Going by its name, it rebuilds what the window shows.

label: Window itself
summary: The event window itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: 2D effect itself (access)
summary: Gives back the 2D effect data itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Duration
summary: How long the event window's 2D effect plays, as a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 0.0 to decide whether a video should loop; a duration of 0 means it loops. The unit is not documented.

label: Mask
summary: The mask of the 2D effect, as text.
details: Going by its name and text return type; vanilla never uses it.

label: Video
summary: The video file of the event window's 2D effect, as text.
details: Vanilla sets a video widget's `video` from it.

label: Has effect
summary: Whether the event has a 2D effect to show.
details: Vanilla uses it, with a check that no transition is showing, to show the effect widget.

label: Has mask
summary: Whether the 2D effect uses a mask.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch between a widget for effects with a mask and one for effects without.

label: Is texture mask
summary: Whether the mask of the 2D effect is a texture.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it.

label: Is video mask
summary: Whether the mask of the 2D effect is a video.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it.

label: 2D effect itself
summary: The 2D effect data itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Background itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event background data itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Environment
summary: The environment of the event background.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `GetEnvironment` of a similar activity type when drawing an animated portrait; nothing uses this one.

label: Texture
summary: The texture (picture) of the event window's background.
details: Vanilla sets the `texture` of the background in the event window's visual effect widgets from it.

label: Video
summary: The video file of the event window's background, as text.
details: Vanilla sets a video widget's `video` from it.

label: Video mask
summary: The mask video file for the event window's background video, as text.
details: Vanilla sets a video widget's `video` from it.

label: Has video
summary: Whether the event background has a video.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose between a video, a masked video and a still background.

label: Has video mask
summary: Whether the event background has a video mask.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose between a video, a masked video and a still background.

label: Background itself
summary: The event background data itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Situation widget itself (access)
summary: Gives back the situation info widget data itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Situation
summary: The situation that the event window's situation info widget is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the situation widgets (the general one, the Christian church one, the dynastic cycle one and others).

label: Situation widget itself
summary: The situation info widget data itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Struggle widget itself (access)
summary: Gives back the struggle info widget data itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Struggle
summary: The struggle that the event window's struggle info widget is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the struggle widget.

label: Is start event
summary: Whether the event shown is the one that starts the struggle.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show different parts of the struggle widget.

label: Struggle widget itself
summary: The struggle info widget data itself, as an object that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and by vanilla's uses of `.Self` on other types, it returns the object it is called on. No use with this type exists.

label: Background search list
summary: The search list used to pick an event background in the event window's tool.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file. Going by the name, it belongs to a developer tool.

label: 2D effect search list
summary: The search list used to pick a 2D effect in the event window's tool.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file. Going by the name, it belongs to a developer tool.

label: Portrait tool
summary: The portrait tool data for one portrait character of the event window.
details: Vanilla passes it the character entry, `EventWindowDataPortraitCharacter.Self`, and uses the result as a data context in the shared event window file. It belongs to a developer tool by its name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait character entry to give the tool for.

label: Window data itself (access)
summary: Gives back the event window data itself, for passing it on to another part of the interface.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use of the same name on other types, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Theme search list
summary: The search list used to pick an event theme in the event window's tool.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file. Going by the name, it belongs to a developer tool.

label: Visual effect search list
summary: The search list used to pick an event window visual effect widget in the event window's tool.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file. Going by the name, it belongs to a developer tool.

label: Copy text to clipboard
summary: Copies a given text to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla uses it on buttons of the event window tool, to copy lines like `theme = ...` or `camera = ...`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a text, in vanilla often built with `Concatenate`

label: Copy to clipboard
summary: Copies the event window's own data to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla runs it on button clicks in the event windows. What exactly is copied is not documented.

label: Debug open
summary: Opens a debug view of the event.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click or right click of debug buttons in the event windows. What the view shows is not documented.

label: Animated portrait texture
summary: The animated portrait picture for one portrait position of the event, drawn with a given camera and size.
details: Vanilla calls it with a position name ('left_portrait', 'center_portrait', 'right_portrait'), a camera name ('camera_event_left', 'camera_event_right') and the widget's screen size.

label: Animation tool text
summary: The text line for an animation, as the event window tool builds it for a selected entry.
details: Vanilla gives it the selected text of a search list, and uses the result as a tooltip and as the text copied to the clipboard.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: in vanilla the selected text of the tool's list

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact shown at a given portrait position of the event.
details: Vanilla gives it a position name such as 'lower_left_portrait', 'lower_center_portrait' or 'lower_right_portrait', and uses the result as a data context.

label: Content source DLC
summary: The DLC that the event comes from.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the tooltip "This Event is from '<DLC>'", and uses its event decoration (an image) in the big event window.

label: Days remaining
summary: The number of days left before an option is picked automatically.
details: Vanilla shows it in multiplayer warnings ("this option will be picked automatically in N days") and compares it with 30 to decide when to show them.

label: Debug info
summary: A debug text about the event, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip of a debug button in the event windows.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the event, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the activity window.

label: 2D effect data
summary: The 2D effect data of the event.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file, for the widgets that show the effect.

label: Background data
summary: The background data of the event.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the event window's visual effect widgets, and asks it whether the background has a video.

label: Transition data
summary: The transition data of the event, used when the window changes from one scene to another.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the shared event window file. The meaning of the type is read from its name.

label: Immediate effects tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the immediate effects of the event, as text.
details: Going by its name and text return type; vanilla never uses it.

label: Involved characters
summary: The list of characters involved in the event.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that the court events window repeats rows over.

label: Opening
summary: The opening text of a letter event, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the letter and anonymous letter event windows.

label: Options
summary: The list of options of the event.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list rows repeat over in the activity window, and checks how many there are (fewer than 7). Each entry is an event option.
